blocks.heading: Averaged Null Energy Condition
blocks.text: The proposed framework replaces pointwise energy conditions with the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC). The equation above defines the integral constraint on the stress-energy tensor along complete null generators, establishing the baseline energy condition required for the subsequent focusing arguments.

blocks.heading: Assumption Ledger
blocks.text:
The derivation consumes the following scoped premises, defined in the primary definition ledger:
- A1: Spherical symmetry and isotropic pressure.
- A2: AANEC satisfaction along complete null generators.
- A3: Global hyperbolicity and regularity.
- A4: Completeness of null generators.
- A5: Explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition.
- A6: Stable equilibrium bounded by a compactness limit.

blocks.heading: Proposed Trapped-Surface Threshold
blocks.text: The plan proposes a forward derivation (S1-S4) establishing that if the compactness parameter exceeds a model-dependent threshold, the explicit averaged focusing condition forces the expansion scalar to become negative. The failure condition for this proposition is the existence of a stable, non-black-hole remnant that satisfies all assumptions A1-A6 but evades trapped-surface formation.

blocks.heading: Counterexample Decision Matrix
blocks.text:
| Candidate Case | Assumption Check | Failure or Interpretation | Next Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Static regular metric (CE1) | A5 (Averaged Focusing) | Likely violation of explicit focusing constraint required by the theorem. | Verify mathematical form of A5 to confirm exclusion. |
| Regular Black Hole (CE2) | A6 (Stable Non-BH) | Possesses a horizon/trapped surface, thus classified as a black hole, not a non-BH remnant. | Confirm horizon definition aligns with A6 stability predicate. |
| Exotic compact object | A1 (Spherical Symmetry) | Out of domain; assumes nonspherical or rotating dynamics not covered by A1. | Restrict scope to spherical collapse; treat as boundary case. |

blocks.heading: Verification Boundaries
blocks.text: The validity of the counterexample search depends on the precise mathematical formulation of the averaged focusing condition and the Misner-Sharp compactness parameter. Without these formal definitions, the distinction between a valid counterexample and a definition conflict remains unverified. The decision matrix above highlights that candidate witnesses often fail to satisfy the full set of assumptions required to negate the target proposition.
